transcript:
Header: 2027-09-14 | 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Product), Raj Patel (Helix - Dir of Data), Elena Moretti (Helix - InfoSec), Omar Ruiz (Helix - Platform), Sofia Kim (Helix - Compliance)

Summary:
- Demo/walkthrough of Redwood's data-handling controls focused on request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII masking, and the Optimize suggestions for retention vs cost tradeoffs.
- Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for regulated fulfillment messages; primary concerns: PII leakage in request logs, audit trails, and ability to run short pilot benchmarks.

Topics:
- Request Storage Modes (storeless/ephemeral, partial retention, full retention)
- Logging redaction rules and regex-based PII filters + model-assisted redaction
- Console toggles and API flags for per-route retention policies
- Optimize recommendations: batching, kv/prefix caching and quantization impact on cost
- Enterprise controls: KMS/HSM integration, SSO, audit logs, export formats

Action Items (from meeting):
- See action_items metadata above for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: All right hey everyone thanks for jumping on. we'll do a quick 40-ish minute walkthrough and then leave room for Q&A. does the time still work?
00:10 Raj Patel: Yeah good, thanks Maya. We, we got a small group from data and platform, wanted to see how your retention toggles actually behave in the wild.
00:18 Elena Moretti: Hi, from InfoSec side — primary thing is we don't want PII in logs and we need immutable audit trails for access.
00:25 Maya Chen: Absolutely. quick note — I'm Maya, liaison, Liam is our SE who'll demo the console and API flows.
00:31 Liam Ortega: Hey all, hi. I'll jump into the control plane and the API flags.
00:38 Omar Ruiz: One high level: we're evaluating three operating modes: full hosted for speed, dedicated reserved capacity for throughput, and an on-prem-ish private deployment for regulated flows. curious how retention and redaction change across those.
00:50 Liam Ortega: Great question. short answer — the controls are the same surface area across modes; the difference is where the logs live and who manages the key material. for hosted, redacted logs can be stored with short retention; for dedicated we can keep them in your VPC; private lets you keep everything on-prem.
01:05 Raj Patel: When you say redacted logs — is that pre-tokenization? like are we redacting before sending to storage?
01:11 Liam Ortega: Yes — we have both pre-storage pipeline and runtime masks. we run a two-stage approach: first, deterministic filters (regex/email/SSNs) in the request pipeline; second, optional model-assisted scrubbing which flags contextual PII (account numbers mentioned indirectly). some customers use both.
01:29 Elena Moretti: Model-assisted scrubbing worries me — how do we audit what the model removed?
01:34 Priya Rao: we emit a scrub trace line for each redaction event with a hash and context id. actual PII is not stored, but the scrub trace contains a sha256 fingerprint and rule id so you can prove an event happened. the trace is reversible only if you keep the ephemeral decryption key — so by default it's non-reversible.
01:50 Sofia Kim: interesting — can that trace be exported into our SIEM? we need it in Splunk for retention policy.
01:55 Liam Ortega: yes — audit traces are shipped to your configured syslog/Splunk endpoint or S3. you can also route them into your SIEM via our logging webhooks.
02:05 Raj Patel: ok can you show the console? how do we flip these toggles route-by-route?
02:10 Liam Ortega: sure let me share my screen. note: demo account with sandbox data.
02:25 Liam Ortega (screen): In the Console -> Routes tab we have per-route Retention Policy. here's a sample rule set: storeless for /customer/fulfillment, partial-retention for /support-chat (retain metadata no request body), full-retention for analytics pipelines. you can attach redaction rule sets to each.
02:46 Raj Patel: what's in partial exactly? is it headers + request length?
02:51 Liam Ortega: metadata only: timestamps, latency, token counts, and anonymized user_id hash. request body is removed or replaced with a redaction placeholder.
03:05 Omar Ruiz: is the user_id hash reversible?
03:07 Priya Rao: it's a keyed HMAC using your KMS-managed key. reversible only if you maintain the key. we typically recommend rotate keys quarterly.
03:18 Elena Moretti: talk about retention lifecycles — can we do age-based ejection and archive to cold storage?
03:23 Liam Ortega: yep lifecycle policies are in Console -> Data Lifecycle. you can set hot (0-30 days), warm (30-90), cold (>90), and an ejection rule that deletes PII-containing items earlier. ejection actions are logged to the audit trail.
03:38 Raj Patel: any support for selective ejection, like remove PII fields but keep non-sensitive transcripts?
03:44 Liam Ortega: yes we call that selective sanitization: field-level redaction using JSON path rules. we can remove only fields marked sensitive and persist others.
03:56 Omar Ruiz: want to see how that works on an actual request stream. can you replay a sample?
04:00 Liam Ortega: sure running a replay now — playing three messages through the pipeline.
04:15 [sound of keyboard/mini pause]
04:25 Liam Ortega: first message contains an email and a 9-digit acct — see the redaction rule match at 04:26, console shows the scrub trace id. consoles sometimes show small spelling stuff, sorry, the UI text is 'scrubbed' not 'scrubed' — minor.
04:40 Raj Patel: ha, fair. the scrub trace includes rule id and sha?
04:44 Liam Ortega: yes, rule id, sha256 of removed token, route id, timestamp, and operator id.
04:50 Elena Moretti: show me the API flag — we want to set retention per request in our app logic, not only in the console.
04:55 Liam Ortega: absolutely — you can pass header X-Redwood-Retention: storeless|partial|full or include retention in the SDK call payload. precedence is: request header -> route policy -> org default.
05:10 Omar Ruiz: ok, what about redaction latency? we're worried about adding 200-300ms.
05:15 Liam Ortega: deterministic filters are sub-ms; model-assisted scrub adds 20-80ms depending on sequence length. Optimize can suggest moving those checks off the critical path by running asynchronous redaction with pre-signed placeholders if you need 1x SLO.
05:32 Raj Patel: can you explain pre-signed placeholders?
05:34 Priya Rao: it's a technique: we return a placeholder token to the app quickly, and post-process the request body for redaction/archival. you get low tail latency for user flow, then the scrubbed content goes to your secure store.
05:48 Sofia Kim: compliance asks for proof of deletion. how's that handled for retained logs?
05:53 Liam Ortega: when an item is deleted we emit an immutable deletion event with timestamp and operator id; that event is written to the audit log plus signed by our HSM if you're on Dedicated/Private.
06:05 Raj Patel: what about data subject request flows — can a user request erasure and we find all traces?
06:09 Priya Rao: yes we have request-ejection APIs that search across retention stores and redact or delete per your policy. you can run these from Console or call the API; they produce a compliance report.
06:20 Omar Ruiz: can we test with our real payloads?
06:22 Maya Chen: that's part of the pilot — Liam will run a bench with your samples.
06:28 Liam Ortega: moving to Optimize briefly — our product looks at traffic shape and suggests batching (to lower token cost), KV cache windows, and whether quantization would impact quality. it also simulates unit cost changes across profiles.
06:44 Raj Patel: would Optimize flag redaction as increasing token counts?
06:47 Priya Rao: yes, redaction can increase tokens if you're adding system prompts or using model-assisted scrub, Optimize will show you token delta and cost impact per route.
06:55 Elena Moretti: competitors sometimes claim full PII-free logs by default; how is Redwood different?
06:59 Liam Ortega: many providers only do simple regex; our difference is multi-stage (regex + model + field-level rules) plus per-route policy and audit traceability. we also let you keep everything in your VPC if needed.
07:12 Raj Patel: question about keys — KMS integrations supported? GCP KMS, AWS KMS, HSM?
07:17 Priya Rao: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and enterprise HSMs. for private deployments you can bring-your-own-HSM and we never access key material.
07:27 Omar Ruiz: can you show sample syslog payload for scrub traces?
07:30 Liam Ortega: sure — screen share again. here's a JSON line (redacted in demo): { \"trace_id\": \"...\", \"rule\":\"email-01\", \"sha\":\"...\", \"route\":\"/fulfillment\" } — note in real export we'd have structured fields for SIEM ingest.
07:48 Raj Patel: I noticed earlier you mentioned ejection policies tied to quality monitors. can you expand?
07:52 Priya Rao: yes, we integrate with Redwood Optimize's quality monitoring: if a route's eval set shows regressions post-quantization or after a model change, you can auto-eject recent stored requests flagged as low-quality so you can mitigate privacy/regression coupling.
08:08 Sofia Kim: that's neat: so we could auto-delete anything generated under a flagged rollout?
08:13 Priya Rao: correct, auto-eject or quarantine; quarantined items can be exported for human review in an isolated bucket.
08:21 Omar Ruiz: we have a throughput-heavy fulfillment path — would storeless mode affect our metrics or debugging?
08:28 Liam Ortega: storeless keeps minimal telemetry (latency, token counts, route id). debugging harder for content-related issues, but you can enable short retention (7d) for specific canary routes.
08:40 Raj Patel: can we set retention toggles at the biz-unit level, say some teams get full retention?
08:45 Liam Ortega: yep policy inheritance supports org -> workspace -> route scoping.
08:51 Regina (Speaker mismatch/noise): [inaudible chuckle]
08:55 Elena Moretti: ok show me the API call example to set X-Redwood-Retention.
09:00 Liam Ortega: copy-paste: POST /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Retention: storeless and body {\"input\":\"...\"} — if you use SDK, it's a parameter retention: 'storeless'.
09:14 Omar Ruiz: are there SDKs for go/python/node?
09:16 Maya Chen: yes official SDKs for Node/Python/Go and a thin HTTP wrapper for others.
09:23 Raj Patel: pricing — if we do per-request storeless but still use model-assisted scrub for some routes, how is that billed?
09:29 Priya Rao: storage costs are zero for storeless; model-assisted scrub is billed as compute per request (per-token). Optimize shows projected monthly cost given your traffic.
09:41 Elena Moretti: show me an example compliance report after ejection.
09:44 Liam Ortega: sharing an Example PDF — it includes: timeline of events, deletion hashes, operator signatures, and syslog exports.
09:58 Raj Patel: curious about retention granularity: can we set TTLs on specific fields?
10:02 Priya Rao: yes field-level TTLs are supported via metadata templates; you can say 'phone_number: ttl=30d' while keeping message_text ttl=365d.
10:12 Omar Ruiz: latency bench — can you run a quick sequence? not full but an estimate for the fulfillment flow with storeless + deterministic redaction.
10:18 Liam Ortega: quick estimate: median latency adds ~8ms for deterministic filters; model-assisted + 512 token seq ~ 50ms median. we can run a pilot for accurate numbers.
10:30 Raj Patel: security: do you store any unredacted content in backups or logs?
10:34 Priya Rao: backups follow the retention policy. if a route is storeless, no body content goes to backup. for partial we keep metadata backups. backups to your S3 are encrypted with your KMS.
10:44 Elena Moretti: legal: can you produce chain of custody for a request?
10:48 Liam Ortega: yes chain of custody in audit trail: ingress timestamp, routing decision, redaction events, storage event, any ejection events.
10:57 Raj Patel: last set: pilot scope and timeline?
11:00 Maya Chen: propose 2-week pilot: week 1 bench with anonymized payloads and redaction checks; week 2 run live canary on 1% traffic with short retention. we can convert to dedicated if you need VPC placements.
11:14 Omar Ruiz: we need price for the pilot and the cost delta to go dedicated.
11:18 Maya Chen: I'll send a pilot price sheet and a delta comparison for dedicated (monthly commit) vs hosted usage.
11:25 Raj Patel: sounds good. thanks.
11:28 Elena Moretti: a couple more questions offline about HSM attestation.
11:32 Maya Chen: noted, we'll include attestation in the security pack.
11:36 Sofia Kim: one quick question — can we redact PII at the token level vs whole field?
11:40 Liam Ortega: yes token-level masking is supported if you want to keep non-sensitive tokens in the same field. there are pros/cons for downstream analytics.
11:52 Raj Patel: excellent. that's it from us.
11:55 Maya Chen: great thanks everybody. next steps captured. we'll follow up with the security pack and schedule the pilot kickoff.
12:00 [call ends]
